page: Microsoft Azure L8as_v5 is a storage-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD x86_64 processor delivering 8 dedicated vCPUs paired with 64.0 GB of memory, representing an allocation of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware capabilities also support external Azure Premium Storage attachments in addition to its included local storage resources.

A key feature of the L8as_v5 instance is its bundled 1920 GB local NVMe SSD. The direct-attached NVMe storage provides high-throughput, low-latency disk access for input-output intensive applications without the latency overhead of network-attached block devices. The instance includes no GPU acceleration hardware and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From an architectural perspective, combining 1920 GB of local NVMe storage with an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio delivers strong resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for I/O-heavy setups. A key operational tradeoff is the ephemeral nature of direct-attached NVMe storage in cloud environments, requiring fault-tolerant software configurations or replication for stateful applications.

Microsoft Azure L8as_v5 is targeted at transactional databases, distributed NoSQL datastores such as Apache Cassandra and MongoDB, search indexing clusters, and high-performance caching layers that rely on fast local scratch or staging storage.
